title: How much operating cash remained after Apple’s PP&E investment?
introduction: Operating Cash Flow is not automatically free to spend. One common analytical step subtracts investment in property, plant and equipment.
definition: Free Cash Flow is an analytical measure, not a GAAP line Apple reports. Definitions can vary. FinPath uses one simple educational convention here: Operating Cash Flow minus PP&E purchases.

payments-for-property-plant-and-equipmen.reportedLabel: Payments for acquisition of property, plant and equipment
payments-for-property-plant-and-equipmen.helper: Apple reports this cash outflow in Investing activities.

question.prompt: Which value did Apple directly report?
question.hint: Choose one. This is practice, not a score.

choices.label: Free Cash Flow shown by FinPath

question.supportedFeedback: Apple reported Operating Cash Flow. FinPath derived simple Free Cash Flow from that figure and Apple’s reported PP&E purchases.
question.unsupportedFeedback: Apple did not report this Free Cash Flow as a GAAP statement line. FinPath calculated it from two Apple-reported inputs.

limitation: This simple Free Cash Flow is not Apple’s ending cash balance, Net Income, company valuation, or cash guaranteed to shareholders. A positive result is not automatically an investment judgement.

verification.unitNote: Apple reports the inputs in USD millions. FinPath derives the exact result, then displays it in USD billions.

sources.title: Apple FY2025 Form 10-K — Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
